data.title: Opacity
data.tagline: Make an element and its contents more transparent
data.description: Opacity changes the transparency of an entire element, including its children. It can soften secondary or disabled content, but low opacity also reduces text contrast. Use a transparent color when only the background should fade.

use: Fade an element during a transition
Reduce the emphasis of decorative content
avoid: Lower body-text contrast until it is hard to read
Use opacity when only the background should change
Hide content visually while leaving an unexpected click target
Use transparency as the only sign that a control is disabled

lessonPractice.title: A surface needs a translucent background revealing the page behind, while its text and buttons remain crisp. What should be done?

options.label: Apply transparency to the background color while keeping text and controls fully opaque
options.feedback: A translucent color affects only the background layer, preserving content contrast and visible interaction.

options.label: Lower opacity on the entire surface so its background and all content fade together
options.feedback: Opacity affects descendants too, reducing the clarity of text and buttons against the requirement.

options.label: Set opacity: 0 when hidden but keep the surface clickable and focusable
options.feedback: Zero opacity does not remove the element; it may still block the page and receive keyboard focus.

data.agentPrompt: Make only the surface background translucent with an alpha color rather than lowering container opacity. Keep text and button contrast, and synchronize pointer events, visibility, and focus when hidden so the layer never blocks the page.
